content: Azelaic acid gel is prescribed to reduce the bumps, lesions, and swelling associated with rosacea, a skin condition characterized by redness, flushing, and pimples on the face. Azelaic acid cream is used to treat acne. This medication belongs to a class of drugs known as dicarboxylic acids. It treats acne by eliminating bacteria that infect the pores and by reducing the production of keratin, a natural substance that can contribute to acne formation. However, the exact mechanism by which azelaic acid treats rosacea is not fully understood. Azelaic acid is available as a gel or cream for topical application. It is typically applied to the skin twice daily, once in the morning and once in the evening. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Use azelaic acid exactly as prescribed, without increasing or decreasing the dose or frequency. While azelaic acid helps manage acne and rosacea, it does not cure these conditions. It may take four weeks or longer to notice the full benefits of the medication. Continue using it as directed, even if you do not see immediate improvement. To apply the cream or gel, follow these steps: 1. Cleanse the affected skin with water and a mild soap or soap-free cleansing lotion, then gently pat it dry with a soft towel. Consult your doctor for a recommended cleanser, and avoid using products containing alcohol, abrasives, astringents, or peeling agents, especially if you have rosacea. 2. Apply a thin layer of the cream or gel to the affected area and gently massage it into the skin. Avoid contact with your eyes or mouth. If the medication accidentally gets into your eyes, rinse thoroughly with water and contact your doctor if irritation occurs. 3. Do not cover the treated area with bandages, dressings, or wrappings. Once the medication has dried, you may apply non-irritating makeup over it. 4. Wash your hands with soap and water after applying the medication. This medication may also be prescribed for other uses. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Before using azelaic acid, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to azelaic acid or any other medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, supplements, and herbal products you are currently taking. Notify your doctor if you have any medical conditions or if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while using azelaic acid, contact your doctor immediately. Be aware that azelaic acid may cause changes in skin pigmentation, particularly in individuals with darker skin tones. Inform your doctor if you notice any changes in your skin color. If you have rosacea, avoid foods and beverages that may trigger flushing or blushing, such as alcohol, spicy foods, and hot drinks like coffee and tea. If you have acne, you can maintain your usual diet unless otherwise advised by your doctor. If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not apply a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Azelaic acid may cause side effects. Common minor side effects include itching, burning, stinging, or tingling at the application site. Inform your doctor if these symptoms are severe or persistent. Rarely, azelaic acid may cause a rash. If this occurs, contact your doctor immediately. Report any unusual or serious side effects to your doctor or to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store azelaic acid in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture, and do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. Keep all appointments with your doctor while using this medication. Do not share your medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist. Brand names for azelaic acid include Azelex® and Finacea®. It is also known by other names, such as heptanedicarboxylic acid and lepargylic acid.
